claims.head: A tough night ahead for Caulfield
claims.call: The Devils’ P3 (Kovacevic and Chisholm) spends at least 36% of its 5-on-5 time against the Ducks’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Devils keep sending Kovacevic and Chisholm out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Sheldon Keefe has been picking a defense pair for opponents’ third lines. Tonight the Ducks’ third line is Vatrano, Caulfield and McQueen.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 45%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Mikael Granlund is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Luke Evangelista is out (illness) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward. Dawson Mercer has taken his spot beside Timo Meier and Nico Hischier.
Connor Brown is out and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. Arseny Gritsyuk has taken his spot beside Jesper Bratt and Jack Hughes.
Johnathan Kovacevic was added to the roster on Oct 11 and has played beside Declan Chisholm.

NJD.head: Advantage, the Devils
NJD.body: New Jersey will be without Evangelista, but Anaheim will be without Terry, and the Devils have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. The Ducks’ way back in is a penalty kill that holds up.

ANA.head: The Ducks have a hill to climb
ANA.body: Even though New Jersey will be without Evangelista, Anaheim will be without Terry, and the Devils have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. The Ducks can pull it off if their penalty kill holds up.
